hero.heading: @love-rox/ptpt-react
hero.tagline: Split-flap displays for React: `<Patapata>` (one cell), `<PatapataBoard>` (a row of them), and the `useFlipCell` hook. Client components, so they work in RSC setups like Waku and Next.js.

install.heading: Install
install.description: `@love-rox/ptpt-core` comes along as a dependency. `react` (>=18) is a peer dependency. Import `@love-rox/ptpt-core/styles.css` once for the default look.

usage.heading: Usage
usage.description: Render `<PatapataBoard>` with a `targets` string — the cell count comes from its length — and `cellOptions` shared by every cell. Each character flips to its place; the board staggers them. Changing `targets` triggers a new flip.

options.heading: Options
options.description: `<Patapata>` accepts every `CellOptions` field plus the component props below. The shared options behave identically to the Vue, rehype, and Astro adapters.

behavior.heading: Behavior notes
items: Structural options are read on mount — pass a `key` to rebuild a cell with new ones; changing `target` / `targets` just triggers a flip.
`flipMode="replace"` (default) coalesces rapid updates to the latest target; `flipMode="queue"` runs each in order.
The board is one `role="status"` live region; `onFlipComplete` fires after each flip settles.
Pass preset objects (`preset={digitsPreset}`), not strings — a string is treated as the literal flap characters, not a preset name.

related.heading: Other adapters
related.description: On Vue? The Vue adapter has the same API. Rendering Markdown or building a static site? The rehype and Astro adapters do this at build time, with no React in the bundle.
